entities.summary: Thomas Mayne Reid was an Irish British novelist who fought in the Mexican–American War (1846–1848). His many works on American life describe colonial policy in the American colonies, the horrors of slave labour, and the lives of American Indians. "Captain" Reid wrote adventure novels akin to those by Frederick Marryat (1792–1848), and Robert Louis Stevenson (1850–1894). They were set mainly in the American West, Mexico, South Africa, the Himalayas, and Jamaica. He was an admirer of Lord Byron. His novel Quadroon (1856), an anti-slavery work, was later adapted as a play entitled The Octoroon (1859) by Dion Boucicault and produced in New York.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Thomas Mayne Reid's works on American life and colonial policy provide insight into the experiences of Native Americans and the horrors of slave labor during the 19th century. His novels also reflect the cultural exchange between the United States, Mexico, and other regions.
